content.prompt: Find the missing number in the dataset such that the mean is the given number.

answer.short:
$7$.

Multiply the mean by the total number of values, then subtract the known total.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Total} &= 5\times 5\\\text{Total} &= 25\\\text{Missing number} &= 25-(5+5+5+5)\\\text{Missing number} &= 5\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\text{Total} &= 5\times 6\\\text{Total} &= 30\\\text{Missing number} &= 30-(5+5+5+5)\\\text{Missing number} &= 10\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\text{Total} &= 5\times 7\\\text{Total} &= 35\\\text{Missing number} &= 35-(5+5+5+5)\\\text{Missing number} &= 15\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\text{Total} &= 5\times 0\\\text{Total} &= 0\\\text{Missing number} &= 0-(5+5+5+5)\\\text{Missing number} &= -20\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\text{Total} &= 4\times 5\\\text{Total} &= 20\\\text{Missing number} &= 20-(5+5+5)\\\text{Missing number} &= 5\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\text{Total} &= 4\times 6\\\text{Total} &= 24\\\text{Missing number} &= 24-(5+5+5)\\\text{Missing number} &= 9\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\text{Total} &= 4\times 7\\\text{Total} &= 28\\\text{Missing number} &= 28-(5+5+5)\\\text{Missing number} &= 13\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\text{Total} &= 4\times 0\\\text{Total} &= 0\\\text{Missing number} &= 0-(5+5+5)\\\text{Missing number} &= -15\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\text{Total} &= 3\times 5\\\text{Total} &= 15\\\text{Missing number} &= 15-(5+5)\\\text{Missing number} &= 5\end{align*}$$

content.prompt: Find the median and range of:

answer.worked:
Divide percentages by $100$ and each fraction's numerator by its denominator: $12.5\%=0.125$, $\frac{12}{5}=2.4$, $\frac{7}{5}=1.4$ and $140\%=1.4$.
Ordered data: $0.125,\ 1.25,\ \underline{1.4,\ 1.4},\ 1.4,\ 2.4$.
$$\begin{align*}\mathrm{Median}&=\frac{1.4+1.4}{2}\\\mathrm{Median}&=1.4\\\mathrm{Range}&=\mathrm{Max}-\mathrm{Min}\\\mathrm{Range}&=2.4-0.125\\\mathrm{Range}&=2.275\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: $\dfrac{17}{4}\quad 2\dfrac{1}{4}\quad 5\dfrac{3}{4}\quad 7\dfrac{1}{4}\quad \dfrac{31}{4}$

inlines.text: Order equivalent decimals; subtract the minimum from the maximum.

answer.worked:
Divide each numerator by $4$; for mixed numbers, add the whole-number part. The equivalent decimals are $4.25,\ 2.25,\ 5.75,\ 7.25,\ 7.75$.
Ordered data: $2.25,\ 4.25,\ \underline{5.75},\ 7.25,\ 7.75$.
The third value is the middle value.
$$\begin{align*}\mathrm{Median}&=5\frac{3}{4}\\\mathrm{Range}&=\mathrm{Max}-\mathrm{Min}\\\mathrm{Range}&=7.75-2.25\\\mathrm{Range}&=5.5\end{align*}$$

answer.worked:
Using the original dataset, change one $18$ to $16$.
New scores: $15,\ 16,\ 16,\ \underline{16,\ 16},\ 18,\ 19,\ 20$.
$$\begin{align*}\mathrm{Median}&=\frac{16+16}{2}\\\mathrm{Median}&=16\end{align*}$$
Other lists are valid if exactly one original score changes and the resulting median is $16$.

New scores: $15,\ 16,\ 16,\ \underline{16,\ 17},\ 18,\ 19,\ 20$.

Other lists are valid if exactly one original score changes and the resulting median is $16.5$.

content.prompt: Calculate the mode, range, median, and mean. Round to 1 d.p. if required.

answer.worked:
Ordered data: $12,16,16,19,19,22,27,34,35$.

Both $16$ and $19$ occur twice, so the modes are $16$ and $19$. The fifth value is $19$, so the median is $19$.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Range}&=35-12\\\text{Range}&=23\\\bar{x}&=\frac{19+34+22+16+27+35+19+12+16}{9}\\\bar{x}&=\frac{200}{9}\\\bar{x}&\approx22.2\quad\text{(1 d.p.)}\end{align*}$$

Ordered data: $23,38,42,42,52,54,65,68$.

$42$ occurs twice, so the mode is $42$. The middle values are $42$ and $52$.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Range}&=68-23\\\text{Range}&=45\\\text{Median}&=\frac{42+52}{2}\\\text{Median}&=47\\\bar{x}&=\frac{68+54+23+42+38+52+65+42}{8}\\\bar{x}&=\frac{384}{8}\\\bar{x}&=48\end{align*}$$

Ordered data: $205,205,240,240,256,296,310$.

Both $205$ and $240$ occur twice, so the modes are $205$ and $240$. The fourth value is $240$, so the median is $240$.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Range}&=310-205\\\text{Range}&=105\\\bar{x}&=\frac{240+310+205+296+240+256+205}{7}\\\bar{x}&=\frac{1752}{7}\\\bar{x}&\approx250.3\quad\text{(1 d.p.)}\end{align*}$$

Ordered data: $21,23,23,56,66,80,87$.

$23$ occurs twice, so the mode is $23$. The fourth value is $56$, so the median is $56$.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Range}&=87-21\\\text{Range}&=66\\\bar{x}&=\frac{80+23+56+21+87+66+23}{7}\\\bar{x}&=\frac{356}{7}\\\bar{x}&\approx50.9\quad\text{(1 d.p.)}\end{align*}$$

methods: Mode is the most frequent value or values.
Range is maximum minus minimum.
Median is the middle ordered value, or the mean of the two middle values.
Mean is the sum divided by the number of values; use an approximation sign for rounding.

inlines.text: The masses, in kilograms, of the players in an ice hockey team are

children.label: a
children.prompt: Explain why the data has no mode.

answer.worked: Each mass occurs once. Every data value is different, so there is no mode.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the mean mass of the ice hockey players.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the median mass. Hint: Remember to put the masses in order first.

answer.worked:
In ascending order: $89.2,\;89.7,\;93.4,\;94.2,\;95.2,\;98.8$.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Median}&=\frac{93.4+94.2}{2}\\\text{Median}&=93.8\text{ kg}\end{align*}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: Which, if any, of the averages will change if the heaviest player is replaced by a player of mass 94 kg?

inlines.text: The mean and median change; there is still no mode. The range also changes, but it measures spread rather than an average.

answer.worked:

inlines.text: The mean doesn’t have to be part of the dataset, but a mode, when one exists, always is.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Explain why she is correct.

answer.short: A mode, when one exists, is a most frequent data value, so it belongs to the dataset. A mean need not: $0$ and $10$ have mean $5$.
answer.worked:
A mode is a value occurring most frequently in the dataset, so any mode must be a data value. For the data $0,10$:
$$\begin{aligned}\bar{x}&=\frac{0+10}{2}\\\bar{x}&=5\end{aligned}$$
Since $5$ is absent from the data, the mean need not be a data value. This example demonstrates the mean claim; it has no mode under the booklet’s convention.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Does the median always have to be a part of the dataset? Justify your answer.

answer.short: No. For $0,10$, the median is $\frac{0+10}{2}=5$, which is not a data value.
answer.worked:
With an even number of values, the median is the mean of the two middle values. For the data $0,10$:
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Median}&=\frac{0+10}{2}\\\text{Median}&=5\end{aligned}$$
The value $5$ is not in the dataset, so the median need not be a data value. With an odd number of values, the median is the actual middle data value.

methods: A mean is the sum divided by the number of data values.
A mode is a most frequent data value when a mode exists.
For an even number of ordered data values, the median is the mean of the two middle values.

content.prompt: Consider the dataset: $10, 8, 3, 2, 5, p$

children.label: a
children.prompt: What value of $p$ would make the mean of this dataset 6?

answer.worked:
The six values must total $6\times6=36$.

$$\begin{align*}10+8+3+2+5&=28\\p&=36-28\\p&=8\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: What value of $p$ would make the median of this dataset 6?

answer.worked:
The known values in ascending order are $2,3,5,8,10$. To give a median of 6, $p$ must lie between 5 and 8, so the middle values are $5$ and $p$.

$$\begin{align*}\frac{5+p}{2}&=6\\5+p&=12\\p&=7\end{align*}$$

The sorted list is $2,3,5,7,8,10$; its median is $\frac{5+7}{2}=6$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: What value of $p$ would make the mode of this dataset 8?

answer.worked: Each known value occurs once. With $p=8$, 8 occurs twice and every other value occurs once, so the mode is 8.

children.label: d
children.prompt: What value of $p$ would make the range of this dataset 11?

answer.worked:
The known minimum is 2 and maximum is 10. Range is maximum minus minimum.

If $p$ is the new maximum:

$$\begin{align*}p-2&=11\\p&=13\end{align*}$$

If $p$ is the new minimum:

$$\begin{align*}10-p&=11\\p&=-1\end{align*}$$

A value from 2 to 10 leaves the range at 8. Therefore $p=-1$ or $p=13$.

content.prompt: Find the position of the median and the median. The data is already in ascending order.

answer.worked:
There are $17$ data values.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Position}&=\frac{17+1}{2}\\\text{Position}&=9\end{align*}$$
The $9^{\text{th}}$ score is $26$.
$$\text{Median}=26$$

There are $21$ data values.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Position}&=\frac{21+1}{2}\\\text{Position}&=11\end{align*}$$
The $11^{\text{th}}$ score is $104$.
$$\text{Median}=104$$

There are $30$ data values.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Position}&=\frac{30+1}{2}\\\text{Position}&=15.5\end{align*}$$
The $15^{\text{th}}$ and $16^{\text{th}}$ scores are $24$ and $29$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Median}&=\frac{24+29}{2}\\\text{Median}&=26.5\end{align*}$$

There are $34$ data values.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Position}&=\frac{34+1}{2}\\\text{Position}&=17.5\end{align*}$$
The $17^{\text{th}}$ and $18^{\text{th}}$ scores are both $590$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Median}&=\frac{590+590}{2}\\\text{Median}&=590\end{align*}$$

entries.description:
Consider the following dataset.  1  5  9  10  15
Suppose a new value, x, is added to this dataset, giving the following.
1  5  9  10  15  x
It is known that x is greater than 15. It is also known that the difference between the means of the two datasets is equal to ten times the difference between the medians of the two datasets.
Calculate the value of x.

expectedAnswer.method: The original median is 9. Since x > 15, the new median is (9 + 10)/2 = 9.5, giving a difference of 0.5. The means therefore differ by 10 × 0.5 = 5. The original total is 40 and mean is 40/5 = 8. Adding x > 15 increases the mean, so the new mean is 13. Thus 13 = (40 + x)/6, 78 = 40 + x and x = 38. This satisfies x > 15.
